title: American Civil War
summary: After Abraham Lincoln won the 1860 election, seven slave states seceded and formed the Confederacy; four more joined after Confederate forces fired on Fort Sumter in April 1861. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers died in battle or of disease before Robert E. Lee surrendered at Appomattox in April 1865. The Union survived. The Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 and the Thirteenth Amendment of 1865 ended slavery in the United States.

uncertainty.note: Hostilities began at Fort Sumter on 12 April 1861. The end date is Lee's surrender at Appomattox on 9 April 1865.

as_recorded.value: Confederate forces fired the first shots of the Civil War upon Federal troops at Fort Sumter at 4:30 a.m. on April 12, 1861.

As the fighting came to an end that morning of April 9, 1865, the village of Appomattox Court House lay between the two armies. General Robert E. Lee sent a final note to General Ulysses S. Grant asking for a meeting to discuss the surrender of the Army of Northern Virginia.

importance.justification: Preserved the United States as one country and led to the abolition of slavery there.

audience_note: Addresses military bloodshed, battlefield devastation, and the wartime destruction of slavery in the American South.

related.because: Union military victory in the Civil War enabled the abolition of slavery via the Thirteenth Amendment.
